cli.help:
clat — command-line agent

Usage: clat [COMMAND]

Running `clat` with no command opens the interactive TUI.
Inside the TUI, use `/model` to configure model parameters and credentials.

Commands:
  language [VALUE] Inspect or save the terminal interface language
  standalone       Run the traditional TUI without a background host
  host start       Start or attach to the background host [--trust] [--no-open]
  host status|stop Inspect or explicitly stop the host (--port <n>)
  exec [PROMPT]    Run one agent turn headlessly and print the reply on stdout
  dsh              Open the TUI as a client of a local DSH web host
  attach           Attach the TUI to an existing CLAT host (--port <n>, --trust)
  serve            Serve the local HTTP+SSE API on 127.0.0.1
  history          Search committed session history
  jobs             Inspect background jobs and output
  schedule         Manage explicitly authorized scheduled work
  web              Inspect or configure native web access
  wechat           Bind, inspect, pair, or unbind the official WeChat channel
  plugin           Inspect, install, update, roll back, or remove plugins
  demo             Run the deterministic model → tool → model loop
  upgrade          Upgrade to the latest GitHub release

Options:
  --lang <VALUE>   Interface language: system, en, zh-Hans, zh-Hant (before COMMAND)
  -h, --help       Print help
  -V, --version    Print version

Serve options:
  --no-open        Print the URL without opening the system browser
  --port <n>       Port to bind on 127.0.0.1 (default 2691; 0 = pick free)
  --token <t>      Temporary auth token (default: ~/.clat/web-token)
  --rotate-token   Replace the persistent web token and revoke old clients
  --im wechat      Host the explicitly configured WeChat IM frontend (default off)

Exec options:
  --continue       Continue the project's most recent session
  --session <id>   Continue a specific session
  --command <cmd>  Run one /command headlessly (e.g. --command /compact)
  --trust          Trust the current project without the TUI prompt
  --yes            Approve every side-effecting tool call (dangerous)
  --quiet          Suppress stderr status output (assistant text only)
  --json           Print the RunEvent stream as NDJSON on stdout instead of text
  Piped stdin is used as the prompt, or as context when PROMPT is also present.

cli.market_help:
Usage: clat plugin market <COMMAND> [--market <URL>]

Commands:
list                                      List installable packages
search <query>                            Search ids, names, summaries and tags
info <id>                                 Show the latest compatible version
install <id> [OPTIONS]                    Resolve, verify and atomically install
update <id> [OPTIONS]                     Resolve, verify and atomically update
audit                                     Check installed versions against advisories

Install/update options:
--version <RANGE>                         *, exact, ^, ~, or comparison range
--config-json <JSON>                      Root package configuration
--config-file <PATH>                      Read root package configuration
--accept-capabilities                     Accept capability expansion
--accept-vulnerabilities                  Explicitly accept known advisories

cli.plugin_help:
Usage: clat plugin <COMMAND>

Commands:
pack <package> --output <file.clatpkg>    Build a deterministic package bundle
inspect <package>                         Verify manifest and package tree
install <package> [OPTIONS]               Install and activate a new package
update <package> [OPTIONS]                Install and activate an update
list                                      List installed packages
enable <id>                               Enable an installed package
disable <id>                              Disable an installed package
rollback <id>                             Swap active and rollback versions
uninstall <id>                            Remove a package and its artifacts
market <COMMAND>                          Browse and install signed remote packages

Install/update options:
--config-json <json>                      Store package-private configuration
--config-file <path>                      Read package-private JSON from a file
--accept-capabilities                     Accept first/new capabilities
